sub.en: Look at the answers. Which small word gives the reason — and which form follows it?

items.q: “Why do you go running?” — “___ keep fit.”
items.why: to + verb answers why. Not “for keep fit”.

items.q: I go on the website ___ a local event.
You offer to write it down: “___ write that down?”
items.why: Shall I…? offers. It is only used with I and we.

items.q: You offer to take notes: “___ take notes.”
A more formal offer: “___ ask them?”

tts: So, how are the plans for this year’s Mandela Day? — Great, thanks! We’re getting emails from people all around the world telling us how they’re going to celebrate the day.
That’s good to hear. So what is everyone going to do? — Oh, all sorts of things. A lot of people are going to make soup and sandwiches and give them to homeless people.
I had an email from a man yesterday — he isn’t going to organize an event. He’s going to spend his sixty-seven minutes reading to children in a local hospital.

acts.title: Sixty-seven minutes
text: Nelson Mandela worked for other people for sixty-seven years, so on 18 July people all over the world give sixty-seven minutes of their day to somebody else.
“I make soup to give to the people at the station,” says Aigul. “Sixty-seven minutes is exactly one pot.”
“I repair bikes,” says Marat. “I do it to keep the children in our street on the road and off their phones. Last year I repaired nine.”
“I read to children in the local hospital,” says Bekzat. “I’m not going to organize an event — I’m bad at that. Shall I read for an hour instead? Yes. That I can do.”

items.s: People give 67 minutes because Mandela worked 67 years for others.
Aigul makes soup for people at the station.
Marat repaired nine bikes last year.
Bekzat is going to organize an event.
Bekzat reads to children in a hospital.

lines.s: We’ve got sixty-seven minutes. What are we going to do?
I’m going to make soup ___ give to people at the station. 🍲

Somebody has to call the hospital.

write.q: Plan your own sixty-seven minutes: 6 sentences. Say what you’re going to do, give two reasons with “to + verb”, and make two offers to help somebody else.
write.model: I’m going to make soup and take it to the station, because sixty-seven minutes is exactly one pot. I’m going to read to children in the local hospital to give their parents an hour off. I do it to feel useful, not to post a photo. Shall I collect the money from our floor? I’ll take notes at the meeting so we don’t forget anything. Would you like me to call the hospital?

speak.q: Say out loud: two things you do and why (“I do it to…”), then make three different offers to help — with Shall I, I’ll and Would you like me to.
speak.model: I go running to keep fit. I volunteer to meet new people. — Shall I write that down? I’ll take the notes. Would you like me to ask them?
